figures.caption: Fig. 2 | Factors influencing initial deposition of lithium in anode-free SSBs. a, Schematic representation of a single lithium deposit in an anode-free SSB under an applied stack pressure (Fstack pressure) showing factors influencing the deposition of lithium, including the current collector (CC) thickness (tCC), the stress in the lithium (σLi), current collector (σcc) and SSE (σSSE), the interfacial energy between the SSE and lithium (γSSE/Li) and between the lithium and CC (γLi/CC), the fracture toughness of the SSE/CC interface (Kc,SSE/CC) and SSE itself

figures.caption: Fig. 3 | Factors affecting the charge/discharge cycling behaviour of anode-free SSBs. a, An anode-free SSB after initial plating with a lithium layer of constant thickness. b, Spatially uniform stripping across the interface at relatively low current densities will lead to homogeneous lithium removal and can enable long cycle life. c, Stripping at relatively high current densities can cause voids to form at the interface (similar to lithium-excess cells), which can concentrate current to cause filament growth during the subsequent plating
